paragraphs: The XJ 3.0 V6 Supercharged uses the AJ126 — a 3.0-litre supercharged V6 petrol engine. It was fitted from 2013 to 2019 across the X351 generation of the XJ, which ran from 2009 to 2019. The AJ126 is a derivative of the AJ133 V8, effectively a V8 with two cylinders removed, and shares much of its architecture. The XJ 3.0 V6 was introduced as a more efficient alternative to the V8, offering strong performance with lower running costs. The XJ 3.0 V6 is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road. Jaguar XJ 3.0 V6 Engine Compatibility Because the AJ126 is a specific engine code used only in certain XJ models, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming a V8 part will work — risks a compatibility problem. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact engine code (AJ126) via registration or VIN - Your generation (X351) - Drivetrain and ancillary specification - Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic XJ quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car. cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the XJ 3.0 V6 Supercharged from 2023 to present. The engine features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older engine V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every engine rebuild.
